AN ACT to amend the civil service law, the public authorities law and the

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5487

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil service law, the public authorities law and
the military law, in relation to the suspension or demotion upon the
abolition or reduction of noncompetitive or labor class positions in the
state service; and to repeal certain provisions of the civil service law
relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

Click here

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivisions 1, 1-a, 1-b, 1-c, 1-d, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7,
subparagraph 1 of paragraph (b) of subdivision 7-a and subdivision 9 of
Section 80 of the Civil Service Law.

Section 2 repeals Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law.

Section 3 amends subdivision 1 of Section 81 of the Civil Service Law to
remove the reference to Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law.

Section 4 amends subdivisions 1 and 5 of Section 81-a of the Civil
Service Law by removing references to Section 80-a of the Civil Service
Law, and replacing language with gender-neutral language.

Section 5 amends subdivision 1 of Section 81-b of the Civil Service Law
by removing references to Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law, and
replacing language with gender-neutral language.

Section 6 amends subdivision 7 of Section 85 of the Civil Service Law
replaces language with gender-neutral language.

Section 7 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 3 of Section 131 of the
Civil Service Law to remove the reference to Section 80-a of the Civil
Service Law, and replace language with gender-neutral language.

Section 8 amends paragraph (e) of subdivision 11 and paragraph (f) of
subdivision 13 of Section 3556 of the Public Authorities Law by removing
references to Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law, and replacing
language with gender-neutral language.

Section 9 subdivision 10-b of Section 243 of the Military Law to remove
the reference to Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law.

Section 10 states that this bill shall not be construed to abolish or
diminish the positions for employees in the noncompetitive class or the
labor class which employees are afforded through a bona fide collective
bargaining agreement.

Section 11 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


The New York State Constitution (Article V, Section 6) provides for
filling of State and local government positions via merit and fitness to
be ascertained as far as practical by competitive examination.  Posi-
tions included in this group are classified in the Competitive Jurisdic-
tional Classification (Section 44 of the Civil Service Law).

State and local government Civil Service Administrations are also
permitted to designate certain positions on the Non-Competitive (Section
42) and Labor (Section 43) jurisdiction classifications if the positions
meet certain classification qualifications.

In the event of the need to reduce positions in the State Executive
Branch or local governments the Section 80 of the New York State Civil
Service Law provides a system of reduction in force that affects perma-
nently appointed employees occupying positions in the competitive class.
Also Section 80-a of the Civil Service Law provides reduction in force
provisions for permanently appointed employees occupying Non-Competitive
Class positions in the State Executive Branch only.

There are no statutory provisions that provide this protection to
employees in the Labor Class.

Sections 81, 81-a and 81-b of the Civil Service Law provide a method of
recall via various preferred hiring lists containing the names of
employees who have been displaced from their permanent positions.  These
recall lists also apply to non-competitive class employees displaced
from the State Executive Branch positions only.

Section 85 provides permanent appointments in the competitive class and
certain non-competitive class positions in the State Executive Branch
only.

Employees who are appointed permanently to public sector positions dedi-
cate themselves to public service and as such deserve to be treated with
dignity and respect in the unfortunate event of a reduction in force.

Reduction in Force provisions that cover public sector positions should
not be restricted to the Competitive Class or the Non Competitive Class
in only the State Executive Branch. These protections should be extended
to cover all employees who are appointed permanently to a position in
the Competitive, Non-Competitive, or Labor Jurisdictional Classifica-
tions.

When the State and/or local governments decide to fill vacancies after a
reduction in force has occurred, permanent employees who were displaced
via the reduction in force should be given preference in filling these
vacancies before any other eligible list (in the case of the Competitive
Class) or other non-competitive class candidates are appointed.

This bill sets up the current reduction in force and recall procedure
for non-competitive and labor class employees who work for the State
Executive Branch or a local government employer.

The application of these protections to Non-Competitive and Labor class
employees in State and local governments is long overdue. There is no
logical reason to continue this inequity. The passage and implementation
of this bill will provide New York State and local governments with a

uniform and orderly approach to reducing the workforce and in the rehir-
ing methods used by using length of service as a determining factor.

Employees who have longer permanent service with their employer should
have greater retention rights than those employees who are subsequently
hired to positions in the same title. Length of permanent service should
be recognized in times of reductions in force and rehiring.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law.

summary: Conforms the suspension or demotion upon the abolition or reduction of non-competitive or labor class positions in the state service with such treatment for competitive class positions.
